# Gouda Studios Agent Tools (full)

Pay per event, with no platform usage fee added. AI agents can pay per run through Apify agentic payments (x402, Skyfire) with no Apify account, or call the tools with an Apify API token, or through the Apify MCP server at https://mcp.apify.com. One-URL MCP endpoint for all tools: https://gouda-studios-agent-tools.vercel.app/mcp (Streamable HTTP, Apify OAuth or Bearer Apify token).
Contact: m0f@mail.grokbot.com


## SAM.gov Contract Opportunities

Get new federal contract opportunities from SAM.gov as clean JSON, no API key needed. Filter by keyword, NAICS, set-aside, notice type, agency and state. Includes deadlines, days left and contracting officer contacts. Monitor mode returns only new notices.

Apify: https://apify.com/gouda_studios/sam-gov-opportunities-feed
Actor ID for MCP: gouda_studios/sam-gov-opportunities-feed
Pricing: $0.001 per run start + $0.002 per opportunity, no platform usage fee.

Use cases:
- Small businesses and 8(a), HUBZone, SDVOSB and WOSB firms watching set-asides in their NAICS codes
- Bid and capture teams building a daily opportunity pipeline
- GovCon consultants running alerts for many clients
- AI agents answering which federal RFPs are open for a capability

Input parameters:
- keywords (string): Optional free-text search over SAM.gov notice titles and text, e.g. "cybersecurity" or "janitorial services". Leave empty to return all notices that match the other filters.
- naicsCodes (array, default []): Optional list of 6-digit NAICS industry codes (strings), e.g. ["541511","541512"]. A notice matches if it has any of them. Empty = all industries.
- noticeTypes (array, default []): Optional list of notice type codes: o=Solicitation, k=Combined Synopsis/Solicitation, p=Presolicitation, r=Sources Sought, s=Special Notice, a=Award Notice, u=Justification, i=Intent to Bundle, g=Surplus sale. Empty = all types.
- setAsides (array, default []): Optional small-business set-aside codes, e.g. ["SBA","8A","SDVOSBC","WOSB","HZC"]. Empty = any set-aside or none.
- states (array, default []): Optional 2-letter US state codes for the place of performance, e.g. ["VA","MD"]. Requires includeDetails=true. Empty = all locations.
- agencyContains (string): Optional case-insensitive text the agency path must contain, e.g. "Navy" or "Veterans Affairs".
- postedWithinDays (integer, default 0): Only notices posted or updated in the last N days. 0 = no date limit. Use 1-7 for daily/weekly monitoring.
- minDaysUntilResponse (integer): Optional. Skip notices whose response deadline is fewer than N days away, so you only get ones you can still bid on.
- activeOnly (boolean, default true): true (default) = skip archived/inactive notices.
- includeDetails (boolean, default true): true (default) = fetch each notice for NAICS, PSC, set-aside, place of performance, full description and contacts. false = faster, fewer fields.
- includeContacts (boolean, default true): true (default) = include the contracting officer work name, email and phone published on the notice.
- onlyNew (boolean, default false): true = return only notices not delivered in an earlier run with the same filters (state is kept between runs). Use with a schedule for an alert feed.
- maxResults (integer, default 100): Maximum rows to return (1-10000). You are charged per row returned, so this caps the cost: 100 rows = $0.20 at $0.002/row.
- apiKey (string): Optional. Your own free api.sam.gov public API key; when set, the Actor reads the official SAM.gov Opportunities API instead of the public search feed.

Output fields: noticeId, title, solicitationNumber, noticeType, noticeTypeCode, department, subTier, office, agencyPath, postedDate, modifiedDate, responseDeadline, daysUntilResponse, naicsCodes, pscCode, setAside, placeOfPerformanceCity, placeOfPerformanceState, placeOfPerformanceCountry, awardee, awardAmount, awardDate, isActive, isCanceled, description, contacts, url, detailFetched, source, scrapedAt

Example input:
```json
{
  "keywords": "cybersecurity",
  "naicsCodes": [
    "541512"
  ],
  "setAsides": [
    "SBA"
  ],
  "postedWithinDays": 7,
  "maxResults": 25
}
```

Call:
```bash
curl -X POST "https://api.apify.com/v2/acts/gouda_studios~sam-gov-opportunities-feed/run-sync-get-dataset-items?token=$APIFY_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"keywords": "cybersecurity", "naicsCodes": ["541512"], "setAsides": ["SBA"], "postedWithinDays": 7, "maxResults": 25}'
```

Sample output row:
```json
{
  "noticeId": "9918efd75fd242f387fb70316e0a71ab",
  "title": "GA-VGMS-33528",
  "solicitationNumber": "27M-638A-VA",
  "noticeType": "Sources Sought",
  "noticeTypeCode": "r",
  "department": "DEPT OF DEFENSE",
  "subTier": "DEPT OF THE AIR FORCE",
  "office": "FA2263  AFLCMC WNMK",
  "agencyPath": "DEPT OF DEFENSE > DEPT OF THE AIR FORCE > AIR FORCE MATERIEL COMMAND > AIR FORCE LIFE CYCLE MANAGEMENT CENTER > AGILE COMBAT SYSTEMS > FA2263  AFLCMC WNMK",
```

## SEC EDGAR Filings

Monitor SEC EDGAR filings by ticker or CIK, including 8-K, 10-Q, 10-K, Form 4 insider trades, Form D and S-1. Each result has the company, form type, filing date and document links. Only-new mode turns it into an alert feed for investors, research and AI agents.

Apify: https://apify.com/gouda_studios/sec-edgar-filings-feed
Actor ID for MCP: gouda_studios/sec-edgar-filings-feed
Pricing: $0.001 per run start + $0.002 per filing, no platform usage fee.

Use cases:
- Investors and analysts watching 8-Ks and insider Form 4s for a watchlist
- AI research agents that need what a company filed this week as JSON
- Deal, IR and compliance teams tracking Form D raises, S-1s and 13D stakes

Input parameters:
- tickers (array, default []): Optional stock tickers, e.g. ["AAPL","NVDA"]. Resolved to CIKs with the SEC ticker file.
- ciks (array, default []): Optional SEC Central Index Keys, e.g. ["320193"]. Leave tickers and CIKs empty to get latest filings across all companies.
- formTypes (array, default []): Form types to include, e.g. ["8-K","10-K","10-Q","4","D","S-1","13F-HR","SC 13D"]. Empty = all forms (company mode only; market-wide mode needs at least one).
- filedWithinDays (integer, default 7): Only filings from the last N days. 0 = no limit (company mode returns the ~1000 most recent).
- onlyNew (boolean, default false): true = skip filings delivered by an earlier run with the same tickers/CIKs/forms. Use with a schedule for an alert feed.
- maxResults (integer, default 100): Maximum rows (1-5000). You pay per row, so this caps cost: 100 rows = $0.20.
- contactEmail (string): Optional. SEC asks automated clients to identify themselves; this email is sent in the User-Agent header to sec.gov only.

Output fields: companyName, cik, filerRole, form, filingDate, acceptedAt, accessionNumber, items, indexUrl, documentUrl

Example input:
```json
{
  "tickers": [
    "AAPL",
    "TSLA"
  ],
  "formTypes": [
    "8-K",
    "10-Q"
  ],
  "filedWithinDays": 30,
  "maxResults": 50
}
```

Call:
```bash
curl -X POST "https://api.apify.com/v2/acts/gouda_studios~sec-edgar-filings-feed/run-sync-get-dataset-items?token=$APIFY_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"tickers": ["AAPL", "TSLA"], "formTypes": ["8-K", "10-Q"], "filedWithinDays": 30, "maxResults": 50}'
```

Sample output row:
```json
{
  "companyName": "LAGO Evergreen Credit",
  "cik": "2043759",
  "filerRole": "Filer",
  "form": "8-K",
  "filingDate": "2026-10-16",
  "acceptedAt": "2026-10-16T13:37:35-04:00",
  "accessionNumber": "0001193125-26-423790",
  "items": [
    "3.02 Unregistered Sales of Equity Securities"
  ],
  "indexUrl": "https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2043759/000119312526423790/0001193125-26-423790-index.htm",
  "documentUrl": null
}
```


## USAspending Federal Awards

Search USAspending.gov federal awards by keyword, recipient, agency, NAICS, state, date and amount. Get contracts and grants with amounts, recipients, awarding agency and performance dates as JSON. Track competitors, find who won contracts and build sales prospect lists.

Apify: https://apify.com/gouda_studios/usaspending-awards-search
Actor ID for MCP: gouda_studios/usaspending-awards-search
Pricing: $0.001 per run start + $0.0015 per award, no platform usage fee.

Use cases:
- GovCon BD teams researching competitor wins and incumbents
- Grant seekers and consultants checking who funds what
- AI agents answering who won federal money for a topic, with sourced data

Input parameters:
- keywords (array, default []): Optional words to match in award descriptions, e.g. ["cybersecurity"].
- recipientNames (array, default []): Optional company or organization names (or UEIs), e.g. ["Booz Allen Hamilton"]. Find a competitor's federal wins.
- awardingAgencies (array, default []): Optional top-tier agency names exactly as USAspending lists them, e.g. ["Department of Defense","Department of Veterans Affairs"].
- naicsCodes (array, default []): Optional NAICS codes (contracts only), e.g. ["541512"].
- states (array, default []): Optional 2-letter state codes, e.g. ["VA","TX"].
- awardType (string, default "contracts"): contracts (default), idvs, grants, loans, direct_payments or other.
- startDate (string): YYYY-MM-DD. Defaults to 90 days ago. USAspending data starts 2007-10-01.
- endDate (string): YYYY-MM-DD. Defaults to today.
- minAmount (integer): Optional lower bound on award amount.
- maxAmount (integer): Optional upper bound on award amount.
- onlyNew (boolean, default false): true = skip awards delivered by an earlier run with the same filters.
- maxResults (integer, default 100): Maximum rows (1-10000). You pay per row: 100 rows = $0.15.

Output fields: awardId, recipientName, recipientUei, awardAmount, totalOutlays, description, startDate, endDate, awardingAgency, awardingSubAgency, fundingAgency, awardType, naics, psc, assistanceListings, placeOfPerformanceState, lastModified, internalId, url

Example input:
```json
{
  "keywords": [
    "cybersecurity"
  ],
  "awardType": "contracts",
  "startDate": "2026-01-01",
  "maxResults": 50
}
```

Call:
```bash
curl -X POST "https://api.apify.com/v2/acts/gouda_studios~usaspending-awards-search/run-sync-get-dataset-items?token=$APIFY_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"keywords": ["cybersecurity"], "awardType": "contracts", "startDate": "2026-01-01", "maxResults": 50}'
```

Sample output row:
```json
{
  "awardId": "47QFCA26F0024",
  "recipientName": "GENERAL DYNAMICS INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY, INC.",
  "recipientUei": "SMNWM6HN79X5",
  "awardAmount": 87754106,
  "totalOutlays": null,
  "description": "ENTERPRISE NETWORK OPERATIONS AND CYBERSECURITY SUPPORT ENOCS",
  "startDate": "2026-06-29",
  "endDate": "2027-06-30",
  "awardingAgency": "General Services Administration",
  "awardingSubAgency": "Federal Acquisition Service",
  "fundingAgency": "Department of Defense",
  "awardType": "DELIVERY ORDER",
  "naics": {
    "code": "541512",
    "description": "COMPUTER SYSTEMS DESIGN SERVICES"
  },
  "psc": {
    "code": "DJ10",
    "description": "IT AND TELECOM - SECURITY AND COMPLIANCE AS A SERVICE"
  },
  "assistanceListings": null,
  "placeOfPerformanceState": "VA",
  "lastModified": "2026-09-30 13:53:41",
  "internalId": "CONT_AWD_47QFCA26F0024_4732_47QTCK18D0003_4732",
  "url": "https://www.usaspending.gov/award/CONT_AWD_47QFCA26F0024_4732_47QTCK18D0003_4732"
}
```


## GLEIF Company LEI Lookup

Find any company LEI number by name, or look up an LEI, in the official GLEIF global registry. Get the legal name, status, jurisdiction, registration number, legal and HQ address, and direct and ultimate parent companies. For KYC, KYB, vendor checks and data enrichment.

Apify: https://apify.com/gouda_studios/gleif-company-lei-lookup
Actor ID for MCP: gouda_studios/gleif-company-lei-lookup
Pricing: $0.001 per run start + $0.003 per company, no platform usage fee.

Use cases:
- KYB, onboarding and compliance checks
- CRM and lead enrichment with verified legal names, addresses and parents
- AI agents that must confirm a company exists and who owns it

Input parameters:
- companyNames (array, default []): Legal names to look up, e.g. ["Apple Inc.","Siemens AG"]. Exact legal name match first, then fuzzy full-text.
- leis (array, default []): Optional 20-character LEIs to fetch directly.
- registrationNumbers (array, default []): Optional company-registry numbers as reported to GLEIF (registeredAs), e.g. a UK Companies House number.
- country (string): Optional ISO 2-letter country of the legal address, e.g. US, GB, DE. Improves name matching.
- activeOnly (boolean, default true): true (default) = skip lapsed/inactive entities for name and registration searches.
- maxMatchesPerName (integer, default 3): How many candidate entities to return per name or registration number (1-50).
- includeParents (boolean, default true): true (default) = add direct and ultimate parent (LEI, name, country) where reported.
- maxResults (integer, default 100): Maximum rows overall (1-5000). You pay per row: 100 rows = $0.30.

Output fields: query, lei, legalName, otherNames, status, registrationStatus, category, legalFormId, jurisdiction, registeredAs, registrationAuthorityId, legalAddress, headquartersAddress, entityCreatedAt, initialRegistrationDate, lastUpdateDate, nextRenewalDate, bic, successorLei, url, directParent, ultimateParent

Example input:
```json
{
  "companyNames": [
    "Apple Inc."
  ],
  "country": "US",
  "maxResults": 10
}
```

Call:
```bash
curl -X POST "https://api.apify.com/v2/acts/gouda_studios~gleif-company-lei-lookup/run-sync-get-dataset-items?token=$APIFY_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"companyNames": ["Apple Inc."], "country": "US", "maxResults": 10}'
```

Sample output row:
```json
{
  "query": "HWUPKR0MPOU8FGXBT394",
  "lei": "HWUPKR0MPOU8FGXBT394",
  "legalName": "Apple Inc.",
  "otherNames": [

  ],
  "status": "ACTIVE",
```

## Website Contact Extractor

Extract emails, phone numbers, social media links and addresses from any list of websites. One clean deduplicated row per site, Cloudflare-protected emails decoded, phones validated, MX checked. Pay only for sites where an email or phone is found.

Apify: https://apify.com/gouda_studios/website-contact-extractor
Actor ID for MCP: gouda_studios/website-contact-extractor
Pricing: $0.0005 per run start + $0.0025 per website with contacts, no platform usage fee.

Use cases:
- Sales and agency teams turning a list of company domains into emails, phones and social profiles
- Local business lead lists: clinics, law firms, contractors, restaurants
- CRM enrichment with one clean row per company website
- AI agents that need a company's official contact details as JSON

Input parameters:
- startUrls (array): Websites or domains to extract contacts from, one per line. Examples: https://www.example.com or example.com. Each site becomes exactly one output row.
- maxPagesPerSite (integer, default 8): How many pages to read on each site, starting with the homepage and then the most likely contact pages (Contact, About, Team, Impressum, Support). You pay per site, not per page, so higher values only cost more time.
- defaultCountry (string, default "US"): Two-letter country code used to read local phone numbers that have no +country prefix, e.g. US, GB, DE, AU.
- checkMx (boolean, default true): Adds a free DNS check that each email domain can receive mail. Flags typos and dead domains.
- respectRobotsTxt (boolean, default true): Skip pages that a site's robots.txt asks crawlers not to visit.
- proxyConfiguration (object, default {"useApifyProxy": false}): Optional. Most business sites work without a proxy. Turn on Apify Proxy if many sites time out or block requests.

Output fields: inputUrl, domain, finalUrl, siteName, status, primaryEmail, primaryPhone, emails, phones, linkedin, facebook, instagram, x, youtube, tiktok, otherSocials, addresses, contactPageUrls, emailDetails, phoneDetails, pagesScanned, scannedUrls, charged, error, scrapedAt

Example input:
```json
{
  "startUrls": [
    "https://apify.com",
    "python.org"
  ],
  "maxPagesPerSite": 8,
  "defaultCountry": "US"
}
```

Call:
```bash
curl -X POST "https://api.apify.com/v2/acts/gouda_studios~website-contact-extractor/run-sync-get-dataset-items?token=$APIFY_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"startUrls": ["https://apify.com", "python.org"], "maxPagesPerSite": 8, "defaultCountry": "US"}'
```

Sample output row:
```json
{
  "inputUrl": "https://apify.com",
  "domain": "apify.com",
```

## YouTube Transcript Extractor

Get the transcript of any YouTube video or Short as clean text, timestamped text, segments and SRT. Bulk URLs, any language, auto-translate. Pay only for transcripts you get; failed videos are free.

Apify: https://apify.com/gouda_studios/youtube-transcript-extractor
Actor ID for MCP: gouda_studios/youtube-transcript-extractor
Pricing: $0.0005 per run start + $0.0025 per transcript, no platform usage fee.

Use cases:
- AI agents and LLM apps that summarize or answer questions about YouTube videos
- Content teams repurposing videos and Shorts into posts, newsletters and blogs
- RAG pipelines and datasets built from spoken content
- Exporting SRT subtitles for editing and accessibility

Input parameters:
- videos (array): Watch URLs, youtu.be links, Shorts, live or embed URLs, or bare 11-character video IDs.
- languages (array, default ["en"]): Language codes in priority order, e.g. en, es, de. If none match, the first available transcript is returned.
- translateTo (string): Language code to auto-translate the transcript into using YouTube's translation, e.g. en.
- preferManual (boolean, default true): Use manually created captions over auto-generated ones when both exist.
- includeSegments (boolean, default true): Add an array of segments with start time and duration.
- includeSrt (boolean, default false): Add an SRT subtitle file as a string.
- maxVideos (integer, default 1000): Stop after this many videos.
- proxyConfiguration (object, default {"useApifyProxy": false}): Optional. Leave off to use our built-in residential proxy, included in the price. Set your own only if you want to.

Output fields: videoId, url, title, channel, channelUrl, status, languageCode, language, isGenerated, translatedTo, wordCount, durationSeconds, text, timestampedText, segments, srt, availableLanguages, error

Example input:
```json
{
  "videos": [
    "https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=UF8uR6Z6KLc"
  ],
  "languages": [
    "en"
  ],
  "includeSrt": false
}
```

Call:
```bash
curl -X POST "https://api.apify.com/v2/acts/gouda_studios~youtube-transcript-extractor/run-sync-get-dataset-items?token=$APIFY_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"videos": ["https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=UF8uR6Z6KLc"], "languages": ["en"], "includeSrt": false}'
```

```json

  "availableLanguages": [
    {
```

## Google Trends Scraper

Google Trends Scraper & API: interest over time, interest by region, top and rising related queries and topics, keyword comparison (up to 5) and trending searches, for any country, time range, category or YouTube/News/Shopping search. Fast, reliable, $4 per 1,000 keywords; failed terms are free.

Apify: https://apify.com/gouda_studios/google-trends-scraper
Actor ID for MCP: gouda_studios/google-trends-scraper
Pricing: $0.0005 per run start + $0.004 per search term, no platform usage fee.

Use cases:
- SEO and content teams finding rising keywords and seasonality
- Product and ecommerce researchers checking demand before they build or stock
- Investors and analysts tracking search interest as a market signal
- AI agents answering whether a topic is growing, and where, with real Google Trends data

Input parameters:
- searchTerms (array): Keywords or phrases, one per line. You can also paste Google Trends explore URLs; their q, geo, date, cat and gprop override the settings below. Each term returns one result row.
- geo (string, default "US"): ISO code like US, GB, DE, or US-CA. Leave empty for worldwide.
- timeRange (string, default "today 12-m"): How far back to look.
- customTimeRange (string): Overrides Time range. Format: YYYY-MM-DD YYYY-MM-DD, e.g. 2025-01-01 2025-12-31.
- category (integer, default 0): Google Trends category number, 0 for all categories.
- property (string, default ""): Which Google search the trend data comes from.
- interestOverTime (boolean, default true): Timeline of 0-100 interest values.
- interestByRegion (boolean, default true): 0-100 interest for each subregion.
- relatedQueries (boolean, default true): Top and rising related searches.
- relatedTopics (boolean, default true): Top and rising related topics (best effort: Google often withholds these from automated sessions, so the field may be empty).
- compareMode (boolean, default false): Puts terms in groups of up to 5 on one shared 0-100 scale, like comparing them on trends.google.com. Returns one row per group with interest over time and by region for each keyword. Charged per keyword.
- trendingNow (boolean, default false): Adds one row per currently trending search in the chosen country, with traffic and news links.
- language (string, default "en-US"): Interface language for names, e.g. en-US, de, es.
- maxTerms (integer, default 100): Stop after this many terms.
- proxyConfiguration (object): Optional. Leave off to use the built-in residential proxy, included in the price.
- maxConcurrency (integer, default 3): How many search terms are fetched at the same time, each on its own IP.

Output fields: type, searchTerm, searchTerms, title, geo, timeRange, averageInterest, latestInterest, peakInterest, peakDate, trendDirection, trendChangePct, approxTraffic, status, error, googleTrendsUrl

Example input:
```json
{
  "searchTerms": [
    "ai agents",
    "bitcoin"
  ],
  "geo": "US",
  "timeRange": "today 12-m"
}
```

Call:
```bash
curl -X POST "https://api.apify.com/v2/acts/gouda_studios~google-trends-scraper/run-sync-get-dataset-items?token=$APIFY_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"searchTerms": ["ai agents", "bitcoin"], "geo": "US", "timeRange": "today 12-m"}'
```

## Merch Marketplace Counts

For each merch keyword, return result counts and the top 20 listing titles and URLs from Redbubble, plus TeePublic, Etsy and Amazon Merch shirt counts when those sites allow datacenter access. Blocked marketplaces are flagged, never guessed. $0.002 per keyword.

Apify: https://apify.com/gouda_studios/merch-marketplace-counts
Actor ID for MCP: gouda_studios/merch-marketplace-counts
Pricing: $0.00005 per run start + $0.002 per keyword, no platform usage fee.

Use cases:
- Print on demand sellers checking how crowded a shirt or sticker niche is before they design
- Merch researchers comparing Redbubble, TeePublic, Etsy and Merch by Amazon counts for a keyword list
- Pairing with a trademark screen to shortlist phrases that are both safe and under-served
- AI agents that score merch ideas by competition with real marketplace counts

Input parameters:
- keywords (array): Phrases or merch keywords, one per line, e.g. christmas cat shirt.
- maxListings (integer, default 20): How many top listing titles and URLs to return for each marketplace that is reachable.
- marketplaces (array, default ["redbubble", "teepublic", "etsy", "amazonMerch"]): Which stores to query. Amazon is a Merch-by-Amazon shirt count when the filter is accepted; otherwise the general search count is returned and flagged.

Output fields: type, keyword, redbubbleCount, teepublicCount, etsyCount, amazonMerchCount, amazonMerchFilterApplied, blockedMarketplaces, error

Example input:

```json
  ]
}
```

## Adobe Stock Keyword Gap Scanner

Scan Adobe Stock keyword saturation (total, photo, video, generative-AI share) and expand seeds into Adobe related searches plus Google autocomplete. No login. About $0.002 per keyword. 30/90-day new-upload counts are not publicly available.

Apify: https://apify.com/gouda_studios/adobe-stock-keyword-gap-scanner
Actor ID for MCP: gouda_studios/adobe-stock-keyword-gap-scanner
Pricing: $0.00005 per run start + $0.002 per keyword, no platform usage fee.

Use cases:
- Stock photographers and videographers finding keywords with demand but few existing assets
- Generative AI contributors checking how saturated a topic already is with AI images
- Expanding seed keywords into Adobe related searches and Google autocomplete ideas
- AI agents planning a stock content calendar from real result counts

Input parameters:
- mode (string, default "both"): scan = result counts per keyword (gap scanner). expand = Adobe related searches + Google autocomplete from each seed. both = run scan then expand on the same keyword list.
- keywords (array): Keywords to scan and/or seeds to expand, e.g. walking pad, home office, autumn leaves.
- usePublicReaderFallback (boolean, default true): If stock.adobe.com returns a Datadome/captcha block (common on some datacenter IPs), retry the same public search URL through the free r.jina.ai reader. No paid proxy is used. Turn off to fail instead.
- requestDelayMs (integer, default 400): Polite pause between Adobe Stock page fetches. For ~200 keywords, 400 ms keeps a weekly run short and cheap.

Output fields: type, keyword, seed, totalResults, photoCount, imageCount, videoCount, genAiCount, genAiShare, addedLast30Days, addedLast90Days, adobeRelatedSearches, googleAutocomplete, source, notes, error

## App Store and Google Play Reviews

Scrape app reviews from the Apple App Store and Google Play in one run. Give an app name, URL, ID or package and get ratings, review text, dates, versions and developer replies from both stores in one clean JSON schema. No login, no proxy.

- Support teams finding bugs and complaints right after a release
- Market researchers mining review text for feature requests and pain points
- AI agents summarizing app sentiment from one clean review schema

Input parameters:
- apps (array): One app per line: an app name (e.g. Spotify), an App Store URL or numeric ID, or a Google Play URL or package name (e.g. com.spotify.music). The matching app in the other store is found automatically.
- stores (string, default "both"): Which store(s) to scrape.
- maxReviewsPerStore (integer, default 100): Apple's public review feed returns up to 500 reviews per country. Google Play supports up to 5,000.
- sort (string, default "newest"): Review order.
- country (string, default "us"): Two-letter store country code, e.g. us, gb, de, in.
- language (string, default "en"): Two-letter language code for Google Play reviews.
- includeSummary (boolean, default true): Adds one uncharged row with the store rating, rating count and the rating distribution of the returned reviews.

## ATS Jobs Scraper

Get every open job from company career sites on Greenhouse, Lever, Ashby, Workable, SmartRecruiters and Workday in one clean JSON schema. Give a company name, careers URL or website and the ATS is detected for you. Salaries, remote type, departments, full descriptions. $1 per 1,000 jobs, no proxy.

Apify: https://apify.com/gouda_studios/ats-jobs-scraper
Actor ID for MCP: gouda_studios/ats-jobs-scraper
Pricing: $0.00005 per run start + $0.001 per job, no platform usage fee.

Use cases:
- Job boards and newsletters pulling fresh openings from Greenhouse, Lever, Ashby, Workable, SmartRecruiters and Workday
- Sales teams using hiring as a buying signal for target accounts
- Recruiters and job seekers monitoring new roles at a company list every day
- AI agents answering who is hiring for a role, with salaries and remote type

Input parameters:
- companies (array): One per line: a company board name (stripe, openai), a careers page URL (https://jobs.lever.co/palantir, https://nvidia.wd5.myworkdayjobs.com/NVIDIAExternalCareerSite) or a company website (figma.com). The ATS is detected automatically.
- keywords (array): Keep only jobs whose title or description contains any of these words. Leave empty for all jobs.
- titleKeywords (array): Keep only jobs whose title contains any of these words, e.g. engineer, sales.
- locations (array): Keep only jobs whose location contains any of these, e.g. New York, Remote, Germany.
- remoteOnly (boolean, default false): Keep only jobs marked remote.
- postedWithinDays (integer): Keep only jobs posted in the last N days. Great for daily new-job monitoring. Jobs without a date are kept.
- withSalaryOnly (boolean, default false): Keep only jobs where a salary range was published or found in the description.
- atsPlatforms (array): Optional. Only look on these platforms.
- includeDescription (boolean, default true): Adds plain-text and HTML descriptions. Turn off for faster, smaller runs.
- maxJobsPerCompany (integer, default 1000): Cap on jobs returned per company.
- maxJobsTotal (integer, default 0): Stop after this many jobs across all companies. 0 means no limit.
- includeSummary (boolean, default true): One uncharged row per company with the detected ATS, board name and job count.

Output fields: company, title, department, location, workplaceType, employmentType, salaryMin, salaryMax, salaryCurrency, postedAt, ats, url

Example input:
```json
{
  "companies": [
    "stripe",
    "openai"
  ],
  "titleKeywords": [
    "engineer"
  ],
  "postedWithinDays": 30,
  "maxJobsPerCompany": 200
}
```

Call:
```bash

  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"companies": ["stripe", "openai"], "titleKeywords": ["engineer"], "postedWithinDays": 30, "maxJobsPerCompany": 200}'
```

## Chrome Web Store Reviews

Scrape Chrome Web Store reviews past the 500-review cap. Give extension IDs and optional star filters; get rating, date, text, language, version and helpful votes, plus user count, average rating and current version. Free low-star phrase counts. No login or proxy. $0.0001/review.

Apify: https://apify.com/gouda_studios/chrome-web-store-reviews
Actor ID for MCP: gouda_studios/chrome-web-store-reviews
Pricing: $0.00005 per run start + $0.0001 per review, no platform usage fee.

Use cases:
- Extension developers reading every review past the 500 review cap
- Competitor research on low-star reviews to find what users want fixed
- Tracking user count, rating and version changes for a list of extensions
- AI agents summarizing complaints and feature requests for a Chrome extension

Input parameters:
- extensionIds (array): One extension per line: a 32-character ID (e.g. cjpalhdlnbpafiamejdnhcphjbkeiagm) or a chromewebstore.google.com / chrome.google.com/webstore URL.
- maxReviewsPerExtension (integer, default 200): How many reviews to return per extension. 0 means all public reviews (paginated past 500). Default 200.
- starFilter (array): Optional list of star ratings to keep, e.g. [1, 2] for one- and two-star reviews only. Leave empty for all ratings.
- phrases (array): Optional phrases. Adds one free keywordSummary row per extension with case-insensitive counts over reviews at or below Low-star max. Counts cover only the reviews returned in this run, not estimates.
- lowStarMax (integer, default 3): Phrase counts use reviews with this rating or lower. Ignored if Phrases is empty.
- includeSummary (boolean, default true): Adds one uncharged row with the Store user count, average rating, rating count, current version, and the rating distribution of the reviews returned.

Output fields: type, extensionId, extensionName, rating, date, text, language, author, version, helpfulCount, userCount, averageRating, ratingCount

## Instagram Reels, TikTok and Podcast Transcripts

Transcripts with timestamps for Instagram Reels, TikTok, podcast RSS feeds and any audio/video file URL (mp3, m4a, mp4, wav). Native TikTok captions first, built-in Whisper speech-to-text for the rest. Optional speaker labels (who said what). No login, no API key.

Apify: https://apify.com/gouda_studios/instagram-tiktok-transcript-scraper
Actor ID for MCP: gouda_studios/instagram-tiktok-transcript-scraper
Pricing: $0.0005 per run start + $0.002 per caption transcript, no platform usage fee.

Use cases:
- Creators and marketers studying the hooks and scripts of top Reels and TikToks
- Turning short videos and podcast episodes into posts, notes and newsletters
- RAG pipelines and datasets built from spoken social and podcast content
- AI agents that need what a Reel, TikTok or audio file actually says, with timestamps

Input parameters:
- videoUrls (array): Instagram Reel/post links, TikTok video links (including vm.tiktok.com short links), direct audio/video file URLs (mp3, m4a, mp4, wav, webm, ogg), and podcast RSS feed URLs (the latest episodes are transcribed). An Instagram profile link is treated as a username.
- instagramUsernames (array): Transcribe the most recent video posts and reels of public Instagram accounts. Best effort: Instagram returns up to about 12 recent posts without login.
- maxReelsPerProfile (integer, default 6): How many recent videos to take from each username. Without login Instagram only exposes the latest ~6 posts of a profile (photos are skipped), so you may get fewer.
- maxEpisodesPerFeed (integer, default 5): For podcast RSS feed URLs, how many of the newest episodes to transcribe.
- speechToText (string, default "auto"): Instagram has no public captions, so Instagram transcripts always use speech-to-text unless this is Off.
- sttModel (string, default "base"): Open-source Whisper models running inside the actor. Same price for both.
- maxTranscribeSeconds (integer, default 180): Longer videos and episodes are transcribed up to this length and marked truncated: true. Up to 1800 seconds (30 minutes).
- language (string): ISO code like en, es, de. Leave empty to auto-detect. Also picks the matching TikTok caption track when several exist.
- includeSegments (boolean, default true): Adds segments: [{start, end, text}] in seconds.
- includeSrt (boolean, default false): Adds the transcript as an SRT subtitle string.
- speakerLabels (boolean, default false): Detects the different voices and labels every segment Speaker 1, Speaker 2, ... Adds speakerTranscript (one line per speaker turn), speakerCount and talk time per speaker. No extra charge for the labels. They need the audio, so TikToks are then transcribed by AI speech-to-text (AI transcript price) instead of captions. Best for podcasts, interviews and multi-person videos.
- numSpeakers (integer, default 0): Only used with speaker labels. Set it when you know how many people talk (for example 2 for an interview) for more accurate labels. 0 = detect automatically.
- maxVideos (integer, default 500): Safety cap.
- proxyConfiguration (object): Optional. By default the actor connects directly and falls back to a built-in residential proxy when a platform blocks it.

Output fields: platform, url, author, postedAt, durationSec, viewCount, likeCount, language, transcriptSource, hook, transcript, speakerTranscript, status, error

Example input:
```json
{
  "videoUrls": [
    "https://www.tiktok.com/@brittany_broski/video/7257949160907935022"
  ],
  "speechToText": "auto",
  "includeSegments": true
}
```

Call:
```bash
curl -X POST "https://api.apify.com/v2/acts/gouda_studios~instagram-tiktok-transcript-scraper/run-sync-get-dataset-items?token=$APIFY_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"videoUrls": ["https://www.tiktok.com/@brittany_broski/video/7257949160907935022"], "speechToText": "auto", "includeSegments": true}'
```

Sample output row:
```json
{
  "inputUrl": "https://www.tiktok.com/@brittany_broski/video/7257949160907935022",
  "platform": "tiktok",
  "id": "7257949160907935022",
  "url": "https://www.tiktok.com/@brittany_broski/video/7257949160907935022",
  "author": {
    "username": "brittany_broski",

    "verified": true
```

## Shopify App Store Reviews

Scrape Shopify App Store reviews by handle, with the ratings[] filter, store name, country, time using the app and developer replies. Also returns listing rating, review count, pricing plans and launch date, plus a category listing mode. No login or proxy. $0.00002/review.

Apify: https://apify.com/gouda_studios/shopify-app-store-reviews
Actor ID for MCP: gouda_studios/shopify-app-store-reviews
Pricing: $0.00005 per run start + $0.00002 per review, no platform usage fee.

Use cases:
- Shopify app developers tracking reviews, ratings and developer replies for their app and rivals
- Founders sizing a Shopify app category before they build
- Agencies and investors comparing ratings, review counts and pricing plans across a category
- AI agents summarizing merchant complaints for a Shopify app

Input parameters:
- appHandles (array): One app per line: a handle (klaviyo-email-marketing) or an apps.shopify.com URL. Leave empty if you only want the category listing mode.
- maxReviewsPerApp (integer, default 200): How many reviews to return per app. 0 means all public reviews (paginated). Default 200.
- starFilter (array): Optional list of star ratings, passed to the Store as ratings[] (e.g. [1, 2] for one- and two-star reviews). Leave empty for all ratings.
- categoryUrl (string): Optional. A Shopify App Store category URL or slug (e.g. marketing-and-conversion-social-trust-product-reviews or the full /categories/.../all URL). Returns one listing row per app with name, rating and review count. Parent categories crawl subcategory /all pages.
- maxAppsInCategory (integer, default 100): Maximum app listing rows to return when Category URL is set.
- phrases (array): Optional phrases. Adds one free keywordSummary row per app with case-insensitive counts over reviews at or below Low-star max. Counts cover only the reviews returned in this run, not estimates.
- lowStarMax (integer, default 3): Phrase counts use reviews with this rating or lower. Ignored if Phrases is empty.
- includeSummary (boolean, default true): Adds one uncharged row with the listing rating, review count, launch date, pricing plans, and the rating distribution of the reviews returned.

Output fields: type, appHandle, appName, rating, date, text, storeName, country, timeUsingApp, replyText, reviewCount, pricingPlans, launchDate

Example input:
```json
{
  "appHandles": [
    "klaviyo-email-marketing"
  ],
  "maxReviewsPerApp": 200,
  "starFilter": [
    1,
    2
  ],
  "phrases": [
    "support",
    "price"
  ]
}
```

Call:
```bash
curl -X POST "https://api.apify.com/v2/acts/gouda_studios~shopify-app-store-reviews/run-sync-get-dataset-items?token=$APIFY_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"appHandles": ["klaviyo-email-marketing"], "maxReviewsPerApp": 200, "starFilter": [1, 2], "phrases": ["support", "price"]}'
```

Sample output row:
```json
{
  "type": "categoryApp",
  "category": "marketing-and-conversion-social-trust-product-reviews/all",
  "appHandle": "judgeme",
  "appName": "Judge.me Product Reviews App",
  "averageRating": 5,
  "reviewCount": 49942,
  "url": "https://apps.shopify.com/judgeme",
  "scrapedAt": "2026-11-11T00:07:47+00:00"
}
```


## Spotify Play Count Scraper

Get exact Spotify play counts for any track, album, artist or playlist. Returns stream counts per track, album totals, artist monthly listeners, followers, world rank, top cities and top tracks. No login, no proxy, $0.001 per track.

Apify: https://apify.com/gouda_studios/spotify-play-count-scraper
Actor ID for MCP: gouda_studios/spotify-play-count-scraper
Pricing: $0.00005 per run start + $0.001 per track play count, no platform usage fee.

Use cases:
- Labels, managers and A&R teams tracking exact stream counts for tracks and albums
- Artists checking monthly listeners, followers, world rank and top cities
- Music marketers measuring campaign impact on play counts over time
- AI agents answering how many plays a song or album has on Spotify

Input parameters:
- startUrls (array): Track, album, artist or playlist links (open.spotify.com/...) or URIs (spotify:track:...). Mix types freely.
- maxTracksPerInput (integer, default 500): Caps how many track rows each album or playlist returns.
- includeAlbumSummary (boolean, default true): For album inputs, also output one album row with total play count across all tracks (not charged).

Output fields: type, trackName, artists, playCount, albumName, releaseDate, artistName, monthlyListeners, followers, totalPlayCount, trackUrl, error

Example input:
```json
{
  "startUrls": [
    "https://open.spotify.com/album/1NAmidJlEaVgA3MpcPFYGq",
    "https://open.spotify.com/artist/06HL4z0CvFAxyc27GXpf02"
  ],
  "maxTracksPerInput": 50
}
```

Call:
```bash
curl -X POST "https://api.apify.com/v2/acts/gouda_studios~spotify-play-count-scraper/run-sync-get-dataset-items?token=$APIFY_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"startUrls": ["https://open.spotify.com/album/1NAmidJlEaVgA3MpcPFYGq", "https://open.spotify.com/artist/06HL4z0CvFAxyc27GXpf02"], "maxTracksPerInput": 50}'
```

Sample output row:
```json
{}
```


## Telegram Channel Scraper

Scrape public Telegram channels without login or API keys. Get posts with text, date, views, reactions, links, photos, videos and forwards, plus subscriber counts. Date filter, keyword search, full history paging. $0.0003 per post.

Apify: https://apify.com/gouda_studios/telegram-channel-scraper
Actor ID for MCP: gouda_studios/telegram-channel-scraper
Pricing: $0.00005 per run start + $0.0003 per post, no platform usage fee.

Use cases:
- Crypto, news and OSINT researchers monitoring public Telegram channels
- Marketers tracking views, reactions and subscriber growth for channels in their niche
- Building datasets of channel posts with links, media and forwards
- AI agents summarizing what a public Telegram channel posted recently

Input parameters:
- channels (array): Public channel usernames, @handles or t.me links, e.g. durov, @telegram, https://t.me/s/durov
- maxPostsPerChannel (integer, default 50): Newest posts first. Use 0 to fetch only channel info.
- postsNewerThan (string): Optional ISO date or datetime (UTC), e.g. 2026-11-01. Stops paging when older posts are reached.
- searchQuery (string): Optional. Returns only posts matching this keyword (Telegram's own in-channel search).
- includeChannelInfo (boolean, default true): Adds one row per channel with title, description, verified flag, subscribers and media counts.

Output fields: type, channel, postId, date, text, views, reactionsTotal, forwardedFrom, url, title, subscribers, error

Example input:
```json
{
  "channels": [
    "durov",
    "telegram"
  ],
  "maxPostsPerChannel": 50,
  "postsNewerThan": "2026-11-01"
}
```

Call:
```bash
curl -X POST "https://api.apify.com/v2/acts/gouda_studios~telegram-channel-scraper/run-sync-get-dataset-items?token=$APIFY_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"channels": ["durov", "telegram"], "maxPostsPerChannel": 50, "postsNewerThan": "2026-11-01"}'
```

## USPTO Trademark Phrase Screener

Screen a list of phrases against the public USPTO trademark search (no login, no API key). Returns exact and close wordmarks with serial number, live/dead status, international classes, and flags for any live mark in class 25 or 16. $0.001 per phrase.

Apify: https://apify.com/gouda_studios/uspto-trademark-screener
Actor ID for MCP: gouda_studios/uspto-trademark-screener
Pricing: $0.00005 per run start + $0.001 per phrase, no platform usage fee.

Use cases:
- Print on demand and merch sellers screening phrases before they upload designs
- Flagging live marks in class 25 (clothing) and class 16 (paper goods) for a phrase list
- Brand and product teams doing a first pass on name ideas before a full legal search
- AI agents checking whether a phrase already has live USPTO wordmarks

Input parameters:
- phrases (array): Phrases or design names to screen, one per line, e.g. plant mom, just one more chapter.
- maxMarksPerPhrase (integer, default 200): How many exact and close wordmarks to list. Counts and the live class 25/16 flags still use the full hit set.
- includeDead (boolean, default true): If false, listed marks are live only. Dead counts are still reported.

Output fields: type, phrase, exactLiveCount, exactDeadCount, closeLiveCount, closeDeadCount, liveClass25, liveClass16, marksListed, truncated, error

Example input:
```json
{
  "phrases": [
    "plant mom",
    "just one more chapter"
  ],
  "maxMarksPerPhrase": 50,
  "includeDead": false
}
```

Call:
```bash
curl -X POST "https://api.apify.com/v2/acts/gouda_studios~uspto-trademark-screener/run-sync-get-dataset-items?token=$APIFY_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"phrases": ["plant mom", "just one more chapter"], "maxMarksPerPhrase": 50, "includeDead": false}'
```

Sample output row:
```json
{
  "type": "phrase",
  "phrase": "christmas cat shirt",
  "exactLiveCount": 0,
  "exactDeadCount": 0,
  "closeLiveCount": 0,
  "closeDeadCount": 0,
  "liveClass25": false,
  "liveClass16": false,
  "liveClass25Count": 0,
  "liveClass16Count": 0,
  "indexHitCount": 0,
  "marksListed": 0,
  "truncated": false,
  "scanCapped": false,
  "marks": [],
  "source": "USPTO Trademark Search (tmsearch.uspto.gov public backend, no API key)",
  "tsdrApiUsed": false,
  "closeMatchNote": "Close means the phrase appears in the wordmark, or matches with spaces removed. Not a legal confusion analysis.",
  "scrapedAt": "2026-11-11T00:05:50+00:00"
}
```


## YouTube Video, Channel, Search and Comments Scraper

YouTube data in one actor: video details, channel videos, shorts, keyword search, channel search by keyword, playlists and comments. Views, likes, publish date, tags, subscribers, channel video counts. $0.30/1K videos, $2/1K channels. No API key, no proxy.

Apify: https://apify.com/gouda_studios/youtube-video-channel-scraper
Actor ID for MCP: gouda_studios/youtube-video-channel-scraper
Pricing: $0.00005 per run start + $0.0003 per video, no platform usage fee.

Use cases:
- Creators and agencies researching top videos, views and likes for a topic
- Finding YouTube channels by keyword with subscribers, video counts and external links
- Pulling comments and replies for sentiment and audience research
- AI agents that need YouTube video, channel or comment data as JSON without an API key

Input parameters:
- videoUrls (array): YouTube video links (watch, youtu.be, shorts, live) or 11-character video ids. Returns full details for each.
- channels (array): Channel @handles, channel URLs or UC... channel ids. Lists the latest videos from each channel.
- channelTabs (array, default ["videos"]): Which channel tabs to list.
- maxVideosPerChannel (integer, default 30): Newest first.
- searchQueries (array): Keywords to search on YouTube.
- maxResultsPerQuery (integer, default 30): Top results per query, in YouTube order.
- sortBy (string, default "relevance"): Relevance or most viewed first.
- uploadedWithin (string, default "any"): Only videos uploaded within this window.
- playlistUrls (array): Public playlist links or playlist ids.
- maxVideosPerPlaylist (integer, default 100): Videos taken from each playlist.
- fullDetails (boolean, default true): For channel, search and playlist results, also fetch likes, comment count, exact publish date, tags, category, description and chapters. Turn off for faster, lighter rows. Same price either way.
- maxTotalResults (integer, default 0): Hard cap on charged rows for the whole run.
- channelSearchQueries (array): Keywords to find matching YouTube channels (like YouTube search filtered to Channels). Each result is one channel row with channel id, name, @handle, URL, subscriber count, video count, description, avatar, verified flag and external links.
- maxChannelsPerQuery (integer, default 20): Channels returned per keyword, in YouTube order.
- channelSearchDetails (boolean, default true): Also open each found channel to add its video count, full description and keywords. Same price either way.
- channelSearchAbout (boolean, default true): Also read each found channel's About panel to add external links (website, Instagram, X and others), country, joined date and total channel views. Same price either way. Needs Channel details on.
- commentVideoUrls (array): YouTube video or Shorts URLs (or 11-character ids). Returns top comments with text, author, likes, reply count, hearted flag and comment link.
- maxCommentsPerVideo (integer, default 100): Comments are returned in YouTube top-comments order.
- maxRepliesPerComment (integer, default 0): 0 skips replies. Replies are returned as rows with type reply and parentCommentId.

Output fields: title, channelName, viewCount, likeCount, commentCount, durationSeconds, publishedAt, channelSubscribers, source, url

Example input:
```json
{
  "searchQueries": [
    "home workout"
  ],
  "maxResultsPerQuery": 30,
  "sortBy": "views",
  "uploadedWithin": "month"
}
```

Call:
```bash
curl -X POST "https://api.apify.com/v2/acts/gouda_studios~youtube-video-channel-scraper/run-sync-get-dataset-items?token=$APIFY_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"searchQueries": ["home workout"], "maxResultsPerQuery": 30, "sortBy": "views", "uploadedWithin": "month"}'
```
